overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's account of expression and speech. You'll be asked about the body as expression, sexuality as a dimension of existence, speech accomplishing thought, gestural meaning, and speaking vs. spoken speech.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

options.html: As a physiological drive triggered by specific stimuli
options.text: As a physiological drive triggered by specific stimuli
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty rejects the view of sexuality as a separate drive. He treats it as a dimension of existence.

options.html: As a dimension of existence, coextensive with a life
options.text: As a dimension of existence, coextensive with a life
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sexuality is like an atmosphere, diffused through a life rather than located in one function.

options.html: As a set of ideas and representations in the mind
options.text: As a set of ideas and representations in the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty rejects the view of sexuality as ideas. He treats it as a dimension of existence.

options.html: As a separate function that psychology can isolate
options.text: As a separate function that psychology can isolate
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. On his account, sexuality isn't isolable. It's a dimension of existence, like an atmosphere.

forms.stemHtml: A graduate student starts a paragraph with only a vague sense of her point, and the point becomes clear as she writes. How does Merleau-Ponty describe this?

options.html: She retrieved words for a thought that was already complete
options.text: She retrieved words for a thought that was already complete
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the translation model. On Merleau-Ponty's account, the writing accomplished the thought.

options.html: Her expression accomplished the thought rather than translating it
options.text: Her expression accomplished the thought rather than translating it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Thought tends toward expression as its completion, so writing finished the thought.

options.html: She translated an inner code into written English
options.text: She translated an inner code into written English
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the translation model. Merleau-Ponty holds that expression accomplishes thought.

options.html: She formed a mental image and then described it in words
options.text: She formed a mental image and then described it in words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The point is that the thought wasn't complete before the writing. The expression accomplished it.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are examples of speaking speech, in Merleau-Ponty's sense? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A scientist coining a concept for a new finding
options.text: A scientist coining a concept for a new finding
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This brings a new meaning into being.

options.html: A poet's metaphor that no one has used before
options.text: A poet's metaphor that no one has used before

options.html: Finding words for an experience for the first time
options.text: Finding words for an experience for the first time
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This makes available words say something new.

options.html: Saying "have a nice day" to a cashier
options.text: Saying "have a nice day" to a cashier
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is a stock phrase, part of spoken speech.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Speaking aloud isn't the same as speaking speech. This uses available language.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term for the process by which acts of expression settle into shared, available meanings that later speakers can use without re-creating them? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sedimentation connects speaking speech and spoken speech.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty calls this sedimentation.

forms.stemHtml: Merleau-Ponty says the word carries its meaning the way a gesture does. What does he mean?

options.html: That words always come with hand movements
options.text: That words always come with hand movements
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The point is about where meaning is: in the expressive act, as anger is in an angry gesture.

options.html: That the meaning is in the expressive act itself
options.text: That the meaning is in the expressive act itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! As anger is in an angry gesture, a word's meaning is realized in the speaking, not behind it.

options.html: That meaning depends only on tone of voice
options.text: That meaning depends only on tone of voice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The point is that meaning is in the expressive act, not that tone alone carries it.

options.html: That words are signs pointing to hidden thoughts
options.text: That words are signs pointing to hidden thoughts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the view Merleau-Ponty rejects. The meaning is in the expressive act.

title: Speech as Gesture
